- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% in following period.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), model often lags; add 0.5–1.5% lagged correction to next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates true price if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply +0.5–1.0% bias to forecast mean.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in last 5–7 days.
